question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{4}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{2}+7x+1}{3{x}^{4}-x+5} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{7x}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{3{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{x}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{7}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})}{(3-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{0+0}{3-0+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
